newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - WELLINGTON STAKE CLAIM FOR SEMIFINAL BERTH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - WELLINGTON STAKE CLAIM FOR SEMIFINAL BERTH.

text.p: The Wellington Hurricanes firmly staked their claim for a Super 12 semifinal berth on Friday with a deserved 19-3 win over the New South Wales Waratahs.
A scintillating individual try from New Zealand full-back Christian Cullen put Wellington into the lead just three minutes into the game.
Fed the ball inside his own 22, the All Black backline sensation of 1996 darted around four tacklers in a 90-metre sprint to the try line, scoring under the posts.
Wallaby full-back Matthew Burke kicked a penalty to put the Waratahs on the scoreboard.
Wellington responded with a second try, when inside centre Jason O'Halloran instigated a fluent mid-field sequence that sent flanker Martin Leslie across near the right corner flag.
With their backs in fine form and forwards prepared to play at pace, Wellington dominated the first spell although often failed to convert opportunities into points.
After going to the break 12-3 ahead, Wellington sealed the win half way through the second half. Jason O'Halloran scythed through the New South Wales' defence for a converted try to make it 19-3.
The win puts Wellington into second place on the Super 12 table on points differential ahead of ACT, who also have 31 points.

Wellington - Christian Cullen; Alex Telea, Tana Umaga Jason O'Halloran, Mark Ramby; Stephen Bachop, Richard Jarman; Filo Tiatia, Martin Leslie, Mike Russell, Mark Cooksley, Chresten Davis, Phil Coffin, Norman Hewitt, Mark Allen (captain).

New South Wales: Matthew Burke; Chris Latham, Jason Madz, Matt Dixon, David Campese; Scott Bowen, Sam Payne; Fili Finau, Stu Pinkerton, John Welborn, Tim Gavin (captain), Michael Brial, Andrew Heath, Phil Kearns, Cameron Blades.
